title: Durably record terminal effect and resource refs for a released attempt
description:
Objective: produce the terminality facts `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` requires and nothing in production currently writes. Second producer repair for task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4, per its rail 1: "if it omits a named fact, repair that producer rather than reconstructing authority here."

MEASURED GAP at HEAD fa39721 across apps/daemon/src (non-test). Four fields of `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` (packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-planning-hold.ts:30,33-34) have NO production producer at all:
- `effectsTerminal` — ZERO hits
- `terminalEffectRefs` — ZERO hits
- `terminalResourceRefs` — ZERO hits
- `resourcesTerminal` — ONE hit, and it is `resourcesTerminalRef` inside apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:200, i.e. a fixture, not a producer.

So a reader asking "were this attempt's effects and resources terminal when it released?" has nothing durable to read. That question cannot be answered from a caller payload without handing an agent the ability to declare its own effects terminal.

WHAT TO COMPOSE RATHER THAN REBUILD: effect terminality already has authority elsewhere — the activation ledger records effect disposition, and `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-kernel.ts` owns `SUPERVISOR_LAYERS`. Resource terminality likewise has scheduler-side authority. This task ENUMERATES what was terminal at release and records the refs durably; it must not re-decide terminality itself. If an effect's or resource's terminal state cannot be read from its own authority, that is UNKNOWN and the attempt is not releasable — never an assumed terminal.

Deliverable: a durable record, written on the same production release path as task-740924b741754955b94a7ccf7fc16bb1, carrying `effectsTerminal`, `resourcesTerminal`, `terminalEffectRefs[]` and `terminalResourceRefs[]` derived from each item's own durable authority.

NOTE THE ENUMERATION SHAPE, and reuse the pattern rather than inventing one: `apps/daemon/src/work/in-flight-attempts.ts` (task-48c0c0db) already establishes how to enumerate durable records bounded and index-backed via `readEventsByTypeAfter`, with ambiguity and decode drift refused rather than skipped. Follow it — an effect silently omitted from `terminalEffectRefs` is an effect nobody proved terminal, which is exactly the false-release this evidence exists to prevent.

NOT in scope: release disposition, lease or slot state (task-740924b7), safe-boundary observation (its own producer task), the evidence reader itself (task-e62e3828), or deciding terminality.

Owned paths: one new module under apps/daemon/src/work/ plus its .js bridge and focused test.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "terminalEffectRefs\|terminalResourceRefs\|effectsTerminal" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v fixtures` returns production producers where all three returned zero.

Each ref is derived from that item's OWN durable authority, not from a caller list: a test supplies a caller-claimed terminal ref for an effect whose durable state is not terminal and asserts the claim is refused or ignored, pinning the exact code and layer.

An effect or resource whose terminal state cannot be READ yields UNKNOWN and blocks release — it is never omitted from the list and never assumed terminal. A test drives an unreadable item and asserts release is not available, with the exact code and layer.

Enumeration is bounded and index-backed via `readEventsByTypeAfter` following the shape of apps/daemon/src/work/in-flight-attempts.ts; a test asserts the read count is proportional to the attempt's own items rather than to total project events, with a literal bound a full-stream walk would fail.
`effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal` are TRUE only when every enumerated item is terminal, and a test with one non-terminal item asserts both the flag is false and the attempt is not releasable.
A mutation that skips an undecodable item instead of refusing turns a NAMED test red — a silently omitted effect is the false-release this record exists to prevent.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately, the test leg prints a nonzero count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: This record ENUMERATES terminality; it never DECIDES it. Each effect's and resource's terminal state comes from its own durable authority — the activation ledger for effects, the scheduler's resource authority for resources.
No caller-supplied terminal ref, terminal flag or item list may become authority. A caller may identify the attempt; it may never supply what was terminal.
Fail closed: an unreadable or undecodable item is UNKNOWN and blocks release. Never skip it — an omitted item is one nobody proved terminal, and the list would then read as complete.
Page with `readEventsByTypeAfter` and follow in-flight-attempts.ts's bounded, index-backed shape; do not walk all project events to filter in memory.
Real SqliteEventStore in tests, closed in a `finally` on every exit path. Target <=250 physical lines; commit only owned paths by explicit pathspec.

THREE MEASUREMENTS THAT CORRECT THE PLAN — recorded now, carried into step 2:
(a) N>=2 EFFECTS PER ATTEMPT IS NOT REACHABLE THROUGH THE REAL WRITER. `recordTerminalEffect` takes ONLY {projectId, attemptRef} and derives its intentId from the activation ledger record's single `effectIntent.intentId` (effect-terminal-ledger.ts deriveTerminal); `readFoundationActivationByAttempt` binds EXACTLY ONE activation per attempt (a second is FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS). So a well-formed attempt has exactly ONE durable effect intent. Consequence for step 2(a): the accepted control is N=1 through the real writer, and the multi-ref enumeration arm is exercised by a documented PLANTED second terminal record (planted-row precedent) — the union rule exists precisely so a second terminal record is ENUMERATED rather than ignored.
(b) ZERO-EFFECT DECISION (step 2(d)) IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN: a BOUND attempt always carries exactly one effectIntentId, so zero enumerated effects is an impossible durable state. Semantics pinned = REFUSE (RELEASE_TERMINAL_EFFECT_SET_EMPTY), not vacuous-true. An `enumeratedEffects` count still ships so a consumer can distinguish.
(c) RESOURCE TERMINALITY HAS NO PUBLISHED PREDICATE TO COMPOSE. `ACQUISITION_STATES` (PENDING_ACQUIRE/ACTIVE/RELEASED/QUARANTINED, packages/scheduler/src/authority/resource-model.ts:25) is NOT on the scheduler root — re-measured at HEAD: execution-surface.ts exports adapterConfirm/adapterFail/grantSuccessorCapacity and the TYPE AcquisitionState, but not the array; attempt-resource-authority-contracts.ts states outright "TERMINALITY IS DELIBERATELY NOT DERIVED HERE". Re-declaring a terminal list here would be DECIDING terminality (task rail 1 forbids it) and would get QUARANTINED wrong. RESOLUTION — compose the scheduler's own reducers as the authority: a member is terminal iff NO public scheduler reducer will still move it. Probe per durable row (pure, no store, inputs taken from the durable member only): adapterConfirm (accepts PENDING_ACQUIRE+external), adapterFail FAILED and UNKNOWN (accept PENDING_ACQUIRE or ACTIVE), grantSuccessorCapacity with a proof (moves QUARANTINED -> RELEASED). All four states are covered and RELEASED falls out as the only terminal — derived from the scheduler's accept/refuse verdicts, never restated here. A reducer that throws or refuses AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT is UNKNOWN, never terminal.

The single module measured 299 physical lines — over the <=250 target — so it was split on the same seam the sibling ledgers use ("Split from the derivation for the per-file cap"): release-terminal-evidence-contracts.ts (88 lines: codes, layer, shapes, frozen refusal constructor, `provenTerminal`) + release-terminal-evidence.ts (239 lines: the derivation). That is 4 files instead of the description's 2, which the plan step itself authorises ("split a sibling before 400") and which matches effect-terminal-ledger/-contracts and attempt-resource-authority/-contracts/-reader in this same directory.

WHAT THE PRODUCTION MODULE DOES:
- exact-record admission `exactKeys(request, ["attemptRef","projectId"])` + isText on both, REUSED from effect-terminal-contracts rather than reimplemented -> RELEASE_TERMINAL_REQUEST_INVALID.
- identity -> `readFoundationActivationByAttempt`; non-BOUND relays the binding's own {code, layer} under RELEASE_TERMINAL_BINDING_UNREADABLE.
- EFFECT ENUMERATION: one bounded index-backed walk of EFFECT_TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPE via `readEventsByTypeAfter(type, cursor, 100)` against a captured `readEventHorizon()`, with the in-flight-attempts.ts pager contract copied whole (monotonic globalPosition, foreign event type, no-advance-with-hasMore, nextCursor disagreement, past-horizon break). An UNDECODABLE or non-canonical payload REFUSES the sweep; it is never stepped over. Records for another project are skipped and records for another attempt are skipped — those are not this attempt's items.
- The intent set is SEEDED with `bound.effectIntentId`, which is what makes a zero-effect answer structurally impossible and removes the need for a dead "empty" refusal code.
- Per intent: `readCurrentTerminalEffect` -> ok = terminal; EFFECT_TERMINAL_ABSENT = a readable durable NO (non-terminal, still enumerated); ANY other arm relays the ledger's own {code, layer} verbatim under RELEASE_TERMINAL_EFFECT_UNKNOWN.
- RESOURCES: `readAttemptResources(store, bound.activationAggregateId, projectId)`. ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_ABSENT = zero members (and therefore NOT proven terminal); every other refusal relays {code, refusedBy} verbatim under RELEASE_TERMINAL_RESOURCE_UNKNOWN.
- RESOURCE TERMINALITY IS THE SCHEDULER'S, NOT MINE. `probeMember` hands the DURABLE row back to the four public reducers that own its transitions — adapterConfirm, adapterFail FAILED, adapterFail UNKNOWN, grantSuccessorCapacity with a probe proof ref that is never persisted — and a row NO reducer will still move is terminal. The resulting STATE is compared, not the verdict: grantSuccessorCapacity accepts an unchanged set, so reading `ok` alone would call every parsable row movable. A reducer that THROWS, or that answers AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT (which is what an out-of-vocabulary planted state token produces, since parseRow uses oneOf(ACQUISITION_STATES)), yields UNKNOWN — never terminal. Net effect: RELEASED terminal, QUARANTINED NOT terminal because grantSuccessorCapacity will still release it with a proof. No terminal list is re-declared here.
- `provenTerminal` = no non-terminal members AND at least one enumerated, so a vacuous true is unrepresentable.
- Output deep-frozen including both ref arrays and the refusal's upstream. No Date, no randomness, no FoundationAttemptRecorded, no process exit, no recovery inventory, no absence-as-terminality.

FIXTURE CORRECTION MEASURED DURING GREEN: `runEffectActivateCommand` ALREADY binds the resource set itself (apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-resource-binding.ts calls bindAttemptResources from the ingress), so the suite's own explicit bind was an expected-version conflict — 17 of 18 cases failed with ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE until it was removed. The suite now binds ONLY through the ingress, and the "no durable resource set" fixture uses duplicate resource ids (they pass the claim leg but the ingress bind refuses) with a POSITIVE CONTROL asserting readAttemptResources really answers ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_ABSENT.
